The Breez Hotel · Identity studies · 27 November 2026

Three directions for The Breez

Every emblem and wordmark here is an original vector drawn for The Breez, using only open-licence typefaces as starting letterforms. Photographs are the hotel’s own. The current website logo is a typed “The Breez / Hotel · Busia” in Cormorant Garamond and Karla, with no emblem; the gate sign carries a gold script “Breeze” over serif “HOTEL”. These studies keep forest green, ivory and stone as the foundation.

01
Heritage crest · in the spirit of Le Sirenuse

The Pavilion

An emblem drawn from the hotel’s own garden gazebo — the two-tier octagonal roof with its windowed lantern — standing under an arch, with a breeze line passing through the open sides. Above a spaced Bodoni wordmark, it reads like a house crest that could be cast in brass for keyrings, embossed on stationery or carved at reception.

02
Expressive signature · in the spirit of The Drake

The Signature

A custom script “Breez” — Italianno letterforms, tightened through the double e, thickened as outlines and finished with a drawn swash that leaves the z and returns beneath the word. It carries forward the gold script already on the hotel’s gate sign rather than importing a foreign style. The B monogram holds a single leaf-blade stroke through its bowls. Deep plum appears only where the signature appears.

03
Architectural wordmark · editorial landscape

The Garden Fan

A fan-palm emblem whose blades all lean one way — the breeze made visible — paired with very widely spaced Italiana capitals. At scale the letters become windows onto the hotel’s architecture: the veranda, the tower, the pool lanes.

Comparison and recommendation

Which direction should become The Breez?

01 The Pavilion02 The Signature03 The Garden Fan
Rooted in the actual hotelStrongest — the gazebo is a real Breez buildingStrong — continues the script on the gate signModerate — palms are present but generic to the region
Recognisable at 18–34pxYes (arch + roof silhouette)Monogram yes; script needs ≥ 34pxWeak — fine blades fill in
Physical applicationsExcellent: brass, emboss, embroideryExcellent for signage, menus, packagingGood for prints and patterns
Expressive impact on the homepageCalm, establishedHighest — Drake-level confidenceHigh, but the letter-window trick is familiar
RiskCould feel formal if used alonePlum overused would feel borrowedLeast distinctive of the three
Recommended

Pavilion crest + Breez signature

Use the Pavilion crest and Bodoni wordmark as the primary identity (header, footer, stationery, signage, keyrings). Use the Breez script signature as the expressive secondary mark for one large homepage composition, menus and promotional pieces, with plum only in that composition. This mirrors how a heritage house keeps a crest and a signature side by side.

Header

Small and balanced

Emblem at 30–40px with the spaced wordmark beside it on solid backgrounds, stacked and centred over the hero. Light and dark versions; the crest stays legible at 18px.

Before it goes live

Your decision

The current header text logo stays until you approve. Note: the gate sign reads “The Breeze Hotel” (with a final e) while the website uses “The Breez”. Please confirm the official spelling before any new mark is drawn on it.
